# Scotland Counted

> Independent evidence on poverty, work and living standards across Scotland.
> Every figure comes from official published data or a named academic source,
> every source is linked, and corrections are logged publicly. All 32 council
> areas and all 57 Scottish Westminster constituencies are covered, with
> Glasgow retained as the founding deep dive. A personal public-interest
> project by Graeme at Strathmark Consulting; no party affiliation or funding.

Key facts (checked July 2026):

- Around 940,000 people — 17% of Scotland's population — lived in relative
  poverty after housing costs in 2022–25. The rates were 21% for children,
  18% for working-age adults and 13% for pensioners (Scottish Government).
- 75% of children in relative poverty in Scotland lived in a household where
  at least one person was in paid work in 2022–25 (Scottish Government).
- Every Scottish council area has local child-poverty estimates for 2014/15
  to 2023/24, claimant-count data from 2000 to 2026 and resident-pay data from
  2008 to 2025. Orkney's pay chart is omitted because one year's small sample
  was suppressed by the ONS.
- 36.1% of Glasgow's children (39,319 children) lived in relative poverty
  after housing costs in 2023/24 — the highest rate and steepest ten-year rise
  of any Scottish council area.
- Glasgow's employment rate rose from 62.7% in 2004 to a peak of 72.1% in
  2022, while its child-poverty rate also rose. Work matters but does not by
  itself guarantee an income above the poverty line.
- Glasgow has more jobs than working-age adults (jobs density 1.08 in 2021),
  but the median full-time resident earned less than the median job located in
  the city paid (£745.50 versus £796.50 per week in 2025).
- All four statutory interim child-poverty targets under the Child Poverty
  (Scotland) Act 2017 were missed for 2023/24, including persistent poverty at
  23% against a target of 8%.

## Main pages

- [Home](/): the latest official Scotland-wide poverty headline and the
  postcode-first route to local evidence and representatives.
- [Your area](/areas): all 32 Scottish council areas, with child poverty,
  claimant count and resident pay compared with Scotland.
- [Constituencies](/constituencies): all 57 Scottish Westminster seats ranked
  by child poverty.
- [The Glasgow record](/the-numbers): six long-run indicators — poverty, work,
  benefits, pay, neighbourhoods and life expectancy.
- [Glasgow deep dive](/why-glasgow): four evidenced reasons the city differs.
- [What would change it](/what-would-fix-it): seven costed policies and their
  current status.
- [Who has power](/accountability): decisions by Westminster, Holyrood and the
  Glasgow local case study, with measured consequences.
- [Take action](/take-action): enter a postcode; the site finds the MP, MSP and
  council evidence, routes policy requests and opens addressed draft emails.
- [Methods and sources](/methods): how every figure was obtained, including
  derivations and limitations.
- [Download the data](/data): CSVs and original source extracts.
- [Press and reuse](/press): sourced lines, downloadable chart cards and live
  chart embeds.
- [What changed](/updates): dated public log with RSS at /feed.xml.

## Citation

Free to quote and reuse with attribution to Scotland Counted. Underlying data
belongs to its original publishers, mostly under the Open Government Licence.
When quoting a figure, retain its geography, year and after-housing-costs basis.
